healthcareSystem: Mixed public/private system. Public hospitals provide basic care at low cost but are often understaffed. Private clinics in Gaborone and Maun offer better quality. Rural areas and safari regions have very limited facilities — medical evacuation is common for serious cases.
qualityNotes: Private hospitals in Gaborone provide reasonable care. Government hospitals are functional but overcrowded. Safari lodges often have basic first aid capabilities and can arrange air evacuation. For serious conditions, patients are typically evacuated to South Africa.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 8:30am-6pm weekdays, 8:30am-1pm Saturday. Limited Sunday/holiday hours. No 24-hour pharmacies outside Gaborone.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Gaborone and Francistown are well-stocked with common medications. Outside major cities, availability drops significantly. Bring all essential medications with you, especially if heading to safari areas. Generic names are more useful than brand names.
prescriptionRules: Prescriptions required for most medications but enforcement varies. Antibiotics sometimes available OTC. Carry all medications in original packaging with a doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substance. Carry original prescription and doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (benzodiazepines, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Carry documentation and only the amount needed for your trip.

restrictedMeds.name: Strong narcotics (morphine, tramadol)
restrictedMeds.note: Strict controls. Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription. Declare at customs.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Bring extra supplies of critical medications — resupply is difficult outside Gaborone.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is essential. Most serious medical cases require evacuation to South Africa (Johannesburg). Safari activities and remote travel make evacuation coverage critical. Ensure your policy covers air ambulance and helicopter rescue.

required: Yellow Fever (required if arriving from a yellow fever endemic country)
recommended: Rabies (especially for safari travelers and those in remote areas)
Malaria prophylaxis (essential for northern Botswana, Okavango Delta, and Chobe)
vaccinations.notes: Malaria prophylaxis is strongly recommended for travel to northern Botswana including the Okavango Delta, Chobe National Park, and Makgadikgadi Pans. Southern Botswana including Gaborone has lower malaria risk. Yellow fever certificate required only when arriving from endemic areas.

waterNotes: Tap water in Gaborone and major towns is generally treated and considered safe, but bottled water is recommended for visitors. In rural areas and safari camps, always use bottled or purified water. Safari lodges typically provide safe drinking water.
foodSafetyTips: Food in hotels, safari lodges, and reputable restaurants is generally safe. Be cautious with street food and small local eateries. Safari lodges maintain high food safety standards. Avoid raw salads and unpeeled fruits from informal vendors.
medicalTourismNote: Botswana is not a medical tourism destination. For specialized care, patients travel to South Africa (Johannesburg or Cape Town). Botswana's healthcare spending is relatively high for the region due to diamond wealth, but facilities remain limited.
sources: International Association for Medical Assistance to Travellers (IAMAT)
metaDescription: Health guide for Botswana: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, water safety tips, and insurance advice.

hospitals.notes: Best private hospital in the country. Full emergency department. English widely spoken.

hospitals.name: Bokamoso Private Hospital
hospitals.notes: Modern private facility with good emergency services and specialist care.

hospitals.name: Princess Marina Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main government referral hospital. Can be crowded but handles emergencies. Affordable care.

hospitals.name: Maun General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government hospital serving the safari tourism hub. Basic emergency care. Serious cases evacuated to Gaborone or South Africa.

dentalCare.availability: Available in Gaborone and Francistown at private clinics. Very limited elsewhere.
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Gaborone offer good quality care. Government dental services are limited and have long waits.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, head to Gaborone Private Hospital or a private dental clinic in Gaborone. In safari areas, evacuation may be necessary.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited availability. Some private therapists in Gaborone speak English. English is widely spoken in Botswana.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited in Botswana. Private counseling available in Gaborone. For crisis situations, contact your embassy or travel insurance provider.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is developing. Major hotels in Gaborone have some accessible rooms. Safari lodges vary widely.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Newer private hospitals have basic wheelchair access. Government hospitals have limited accessibility features.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Limited accessible public transport. Private transfers and safari operators can sometimes accommodate wheelchair users with advance notice.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Contact safari operators well in advance about accessibility needs. Some luxury lodges can accommodate mobility challenges. Gaborone hotels are more likely to have accessible facilities.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mandatory mask requirements. Some healthcare facilities may still require masks.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at private hospitals and clinics in Gaborone.
covidStatus.notes: COVID restrictions have been fully lifted. Carry basic health supplies as a precaution.

insuranceClaimProcess: Keep all medical receipts, doctor's reports, and hospital invoices. Most private hospitals and clinics require upfront payment — credit cards accepted at major facilities. File claims with your insurance provider after returning home. For evacuations, contact your insurance provider's 24-hour assistance line immediately.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private facilities. Government hospitals are significantly cheaper but have longer waits. Medical evacuation by air ambulance can cost $10,000-50,000+.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation from safari areas is common for serious injuries or illness. Air ambulance services operate from Maun and Kasane. Helicopter evacuation from remote delta camps available through safari operators.
